proposals.impact: restores daily content output and digest publishing
proposals.observation: Three GitHub workflow runs failed on 7 September 2026: "Daily Blog Post" (08:18), "Weekly Monday Report" (10:44), and "Funnel-Hack Digest" (14:27). The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published. All 24-hour commits are cursor-state housekeeping with zero feature or content output. With the Daily Blog Post workflow broken, the queue will hit zero and stop feeding the email automations that are actively opening well (Money Vigilance at 66.67%).
proposals.proposal: Investigate and patch the shared failure point across all three broken workflows. The pattern — three different workflows failing on the same calendar day within a six-hour window — points to a shared dependency: a changed secret, an expired API token, or a broken import in a shared utility file. Pull the raw logs for daily-blog-post.yml first because it ran earliest and will surface the root error before any retry noise. Once the cause is confirmed, apply the fix to that file and re-run; the other two workflows likely share the same dependency and should recover automatically or need the same one-line correction. Do not ship new copy or queue content until the pipeline can publish it reliably.

proposals.impact: reduces intro-to-q1 abandonment; recovers potential completions from 0%
proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, 3 sessions loaded. 2 stopped at intro_load and never reached q1_shown. Only 1 session reached Q1, and that session did not complete. Completion rate is 0%. The drop is happening before the first question, which means the intro screen itself is losing two out of three visitors. This is not a question-difficulty problem — it is a first-screen friction problem.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro's headline and call-to-action button text so they name a concrete, believable outcome for the ICP rather than a generic invitation. The current text is not available verbatim in the data, so the NEW_TEXT below targets the two highest-friction elements on a typical quiz intro: the headline and the primary button. The goal is to replace any framing that sounds like a personality quiz ("Find out your money type") with framing that sounds like a useful diagnostic that takes under two minutes and gives a named result. Joel's gym-bag moment and the unopened tax-return tab are the kind of specifics that should inform the headline's register — quiet, direct, a little uncomfortable in the way only a true observation can be.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality type
proposals.new_text: There's a pattern underneath how you handle money. This takes 90 seconds to name it.

proposals.impact: lifts Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward Money Vigilance's 66.67% baseline
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance automation: 12 sent, 66.67% open rate. Money Worship automation: 16 sent, 37.5% open rate. Money Avoidance automation: 19 sent, 52.63% open rate. Money Worship has the largest send volume relative to its open rate and the widest gap below the strongest performer. A 29-point open-rate difference on a behavioural-segmentation sequence almost always lives in the subject line, not the body — recipients decide in under two seconds whether this email is for someone like them.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of the first Money Worship automation email with one that is specific to the internal experience of someone who scores Money Worship — the person who ties self-worth to net worth, spends to signal status, or feels a physical discomfort when their account balance drops below a number they've never said aloud. The current subject line is not visible in the data, so the NEW_TEXT targets the frontmatter `subject:` field. It must feel like Joel is describing something the reader has never heard named before. Sultanic test: a thousand coaches cannot write this, because it requires knowing that the Money Worship pattern often sits alongside high income and genuine shame — not greed.
proposals.current_text: subject: Your money personality result: Money Worship
proposals.new_text: subject: You earn well. So why does the number in your account still feel wrong?
